disposition_reason: Risk assessment that reuses lead and cadmium concentrations measured in the authors' 2023 Toxics paper; no new measurements are reported.

study.design: carcinogenic risk assessment using previously published concentrations
study.market: cow milk and soya beverage brands on the Portuguese market (samples described in Lopes de Andrade et al. 2023)
study.method: no new analysis; concentrations taken from Lopes de Andrade et al. 2023 (Toxics 11:1013), originally by atomic absorption spectrophotometry

unresolved: All lead and cadmium concentrations come from the authors' earlier paper (Lopes de Andrade et al. 2023, Toxics 11:1013, DOI 10.3390/toxics11121013), already in the corpus as andrade2023-cow-milk-soy-metals; this paper reprints that data and is recorded as context only.
Abstract gives the highest soya beverage ELCR as 9.12 x 10^-5 but Table 3 lists soya brand 1 at 2.21 x 10^-4; abstract SDs (3.1, 12.1) differ from Table 2-3 SDs (3.4, 12.8).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: US EPA carcinogenic risk benchmark used

regulatory_or_exposure.value: cow milk brand 1.75 x 10^-4; soya beverage brand 9.12 x 10^-5 (abstract) vs 2.21 x 10^-4 in Table 3
